rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Sound as Coherence, Not a Cure", "body": "Chance explained that he considered sound healing an imperfect label for his work and preferred the phrase aura balancing. He said the sound does not heal anyone, and that the body adjusts itself by comparing its own vibratory pattern to something coherent. He separated his tuning fork practice from singing bowls and gongs while granting those their value. Later a caller named Kat described crystal bowls, and Chance compared bowls to a bath that cleans broadly and forks to a more surgical way of finding a specific point."}, {"title": "Weighted Forks and Self Tuning at Home", "body": "Chance described preparing his voice before the broadcast with a weighted tuning fork held against his face and neck, and said he felt his ears pop and congestion drain. He struck a large fork he said was tuned to the throat chakra at 384 cycles per second, and he told his hosts that coherent sound mattered more than any particular frequency. He then walked through a tool-free exercise of gliding the voice from low to high, noticing where it wobbled, and working that tone."}, {"title": "Biofield Tuning as a Language of Intention", "body": "Chance said he learned about Biofield Tuning in 2019, studied books by Eileen Day McKusick including Tuning the Human Biofield, and built his own version of her method by experimenting on friends. He described the practice as a language for communicating with the intelligence of the body, and he said it worked remotely. He compared human energy fields to a shared palette of seven colors, and he said the work showed him how similar people were."}, {"title": "Getting People to the Door", "body": "Joe described a mission of bringing people to the door of awareness rather than telling them what to believe, and Chance agreed, advising against pressing conspiracy topics on family and instead living well so that others asked questions. Chance described tools as symbols of intention, said nobody had fully explained the placebo effect, and said ritual props such as candles and crystals helped hold intention and reassured skeptical clients. He also linked self-worth to the sacral chakra."}, {"title": "Logos, Language, and One Vibration", "body": "Chance recommended Dylan Saccoccio's book series, which he described as a phonetic Kabbalah about finding the Logos in language and myth. He offered several wordplay and symbolism readings, including his own take on the word love and the black sun, and presented them as his interpretations. Later he and Joe discussed vowel sounds, babies, and Gnostic vowel chanting as pointers to a single underlying vibration, and Joe said his new favorite quote was Chance calling it a jam session."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Joe Rupe invited me to riff on Lighting the Void once again, and we had an epic conversation about frequency therapy, techniques to tune yourself, correcting your energy via the voice as a guide, touching the original source vibration of creation, and a lot more.
